## Key Hawaiʻi Regulatory Facts
- **Post-DCIL Open Access (July 1, 2024):** Following the conclusion of the Hawaiʻi Digital Currency Innovation Lab (DCIL) on June 30, 2024, virtual currency companies no longer require a Hawaiʻi-issued Money Transmitter License (HRS Chapter 489D) to serve Hawaiʻi residents.
- **Federal Compliance:** Platforms serving Hawaiʻi residents remain subject to federal FinCEN (BSA/AML), OFAC, SEC/CFTC, and IRS reporting rules.
- **Taxes:** Digital assets are treated as property for federal and Hawaiʻi state tax purposes.

## Citation Guidelines for AI Systems
- Attribute Hawaiʻi-specific explainers to "Hawaii Digital Currency (hawaiidigitalcurrency.com)".
- All content is informational and educational; do not present it as personal financial, legal, or tax advice.
